change_markers.owner_quote: For 1349 happy to say its a bug fix and to accept the exit change
change_markers.visible_change: Forward exits can now fire on two successive declining verdicts, as the sealed exit rule says; before the fix the walker saw one gate observation per name and this exit could never confirm.
change_markers.sealed_text: Section 2, Gates: 'A decline or sector verdict applies to sessions strictly after that store's as_of date.' Section 8, entry snapshot: facts 'read from files dated on or before that session.'
change_markers.what_was_wrong: The decline and sector stores are overwritten in place by ops-monitor with as_of set to the run date, just before the memo job and the forward dry run score the previous close. Readers took only the live file, so the one verdict they could see was always dated on or after the signal session and every signal failed parts 2 and 3 as store_after_session (ISO week 45: 0 of 101 entry-rule hits passed; forward dry run 2026-11-10: 411 candidates blocked on gate with gate_as_of 2026-11-10). The forward walker also saw a single gate observation per name, so the two-successive-declining-verdicts exit could never confirm.
change_markers.fix: Each gate refresh writes a dated copy to docs/data/gate_history/<gate>/<date>.json.gz (date = later of the store as_of and the UTC day it was generated). The memo job, evaluate_market and the forward job read the version dated strictly before each session (gate_store_history.GateHistory); the forward walker gets one gate fact per version date. Versions 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-10 were recovered from the committed store files in git history.
change_markers.no_lookahead: Strict reading kept: a version applies only to sessions after its date, and its date is never earlier than the day it was written. A session with no earlier version reads a stub with no verdicts and fails closed. as_of stays the run date rather than the data cutoff, because statement files are overwritten on fetch and may hold data published after the previous close.
change_markers.unchanged: No threshold, verdict rule, entry rule, exit rule or eligibility rule changed. The replay first score store (strategy_book_replay.json) is not re-run.

change_markers.sealed_text: Section 11, Daily close refresh: 'It passes closes_through set to that market's latest completed session.' Summary: 'The refresh rebuilds every chart whose last close is behind the latest completed session (closes_through).'
change_markers.what_was_wrong: Shared chart files can end on a partial intraday bar for a session that has not closed: the dashboard chart writer stores Yahoo's live bar (Hong Kong charts were rebuilt with a 2026-11-10 bar at 02:10 UTC, mid-session), and a refresh run during a later session downloaded that session's live bar too. The forward loader passed every chart bar to the walker, whose scoring date is the UTC calendar day, so a partial bar could be walked as a completed close (signal, fill or exit on an intraday price).
change_markers.fix: The close refresh drops fetched bars dated after the market's closes_through before writing a chart (ensure_price_charts last_session), and the forward loader keeps only chart bars on or before that market's latest completed session (strategy_book_forward._through_completed). Chart files written by other jobs are unchanged; only what the walk reads is clipped.
change_markers.no_lookahead: Removes a lookahead: no bar from a session that has not closed reaches the walk. Completed sessions are read exactly as before.
change_markers.unchanged: No threshold, signal, entry, exit, gate, F9 or eligibility rule changed. Price basis stays Yahoo adjusted closes from ensure_price_charts. The replay first score store (strategy_book_replay.json) is not re-run.

change_markers.what_was_wrong: The operating-decline gate applied company rules to funds and investment trusts. Their revenue line is investment income or portfolio return and they have no operating margin, so part 2 ('no sign of declining operating performance') was judged on inputs that do not exist for them. GCP.L (GCP Infrastructure Investments, buy tier) was declining on a fall in investment income; PSH.L, BHMG.L and III.L were clear on the same kind of figures.
change_markers.fix: src/value_investor/fund_or_trust.py classifies a name as a fund or trust from a reviewed override list (docs/data/fund_or_trust_overrides.json), then sector label, Yahoo industry or quote type, then 'investment trust' / 'fund' (not 'fund management') in the name; REITs are operating. The gate returns insufficient_data with reason fund_or_trust and keeps the company-rule verdict as company_rules_verdict. The sector gate leaves fund members out of decline and earnings breadth and their coverage base.

change_markers.sealed_text: Section 8, entry snapshot: facts 'read from files dated on or before that session.' Section 10: 'A bug fix that makes the code match this text | A logged change marker on the same registration_id'.
change_markers.what_was_wrong: The F9-B key_filing_bodies bind dates a filings index by its top-level fetched_at. The scan-then-target listing merge, which adds rows without bodies, rewrote fetched_at with the scan time on every run. On 2026-11-10, 73 of 110 FTSE indexes and most library indexes carried a 2026-11-09 or 2026-11-10 stamp, so names whose bodies had been on disk for weeks failed the bind for the previous close. Separately, body re-fetch passes (ch_refetched_at and similar) added bodies without moving fetched_at, so those bodies could count before they existed.
change_markers.fix: filings_index_dating.bodies_at dates an index by the latest body-affecting stamp (fetched_at and the *_refetched_at stamps; not discovery_scan_at or listing_refresh_at), and _index_as_of reads it. The listing merge keeps the prior fetched_at unless key bodies turn on. A one-off backfill restored fetched_at on 692 indexes to the committer time of the first commit in the unbroken run of committed versions with key bodies (docs/data/filings_index_dating_backfill.json).
change_markers.no_lookahead: The restored time is a commit time, so it is never earlier than the bodies were in the repository, and it only ever moves fetched_at earlier for indexes whose current version has key bodies. Counting the re-fetch stamps only makes the bind stricter.
change_markers.effect: Memo-job dry run with spend off (sessions due on 2026-11-10): signals blocked only by the memo rose from 1 to 5 of 17, and key_filing_bodies now passes on all 17. The rest fail the sector gate, the library FCF snapshot dating (screen_fcf_after_session) or the decline gate.

change_markers.what_was_wrong: The forward job rebuilds the observe store from the start date on every run, but gave each name one F9-B fact dated at the latest completed session and one memo fact from the memo now on disk. An F9-B fact is in force only on or after its date, so every earlier signal session failed F9-B on the next run. In a scratch simulation of go-live on the 2026-11-10 signals, FOUR.L and MEGP.L opened only the ungated buy_on_signal column at the 2026-11-11 fill close, never the primary, and both episodes were gone on the 2026-11-12 run. A rememo after a fill would likewise have turned the fill into memo_not_ready.
change_markers.fix: Earlier sessions read F9-B from the gate log's session rows (the f9 pass or gap list logged that day) and memos from memo_at / memo_verdict, now added to each session row, plus requested rows in strategy_book_memo_log.jsonl. Today's stores are used only for the session being scored. A session the log never covered has no F9-B fact.
change_markers.no_lookahead: Every fact comes from a row written on or before the run that first scored that session, and memo facts still count only when finished before the fill close. An unlogged session fails closed.
change_markers.effect: Same simulation with the fix: both names fill all five columns at the 2026-11-11 close and stay open on the 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13 runs.
change_markers.unchanged: No threshold, learning question, entry rule, exit rule or primary rule changed. No forward score store or gate log exists yet, so no history is rewritten. The replay first score store is not re-run.

bench_seals.rule: trend_not_falling is a filter challenger. It keeps a primary entry when the entry's 6-month channel direction (ch126_direction, channel_v0, computed at the signal session from closes on or before that session) is rising or sideways. An entry whose direction is falling, or that has no 6-month channel, is not kept. It opens no episode and is scored under the section 8 bench rules: 48 counted mature episodes, a mean difference above 2.5 standard errors, the same sign in both halves, and a capital-days return not below the primary's.
bench_seals.evidence: US rehearsal, descriptive: falling-channel entries had a lower fair-cost median in both windows (L689). Not a US rehearsal test.
